subproblem.title: Lipschitz extension (Simon 2.1.2) and Rademacher theorem (Simon 2.1.4)
subproblem.statement: (1.2) For every metric space X (Lean X : Type with MetricSpace X), every nonempty A ⊆ X and every f : A → ℝ that is Lipschitz for the subspace metric (LipschitzWith K f for some K : ℝ≥0), there is F : X → ℝ which is Lipschitz (∃ K, LipschitzWith K F), has the same least Lipschitz constant, lipConst F = lipConst f where lipConst g := sInf {K : ℝ≥0 | LipschitzWith K g}, and satisfies F a = f a for all a ∈ A. (1.4) For every n ∈ ℕ and every Lipschitz f : ℝⁿ → ℝ (ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), f is Fréchet differentiable at volume-almost every point of ℝⁿ.
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §1, printed proofs of Theorem 1.2 (p. 40) and Theorem 1.4 (pp. 40-42). No erratum affects these two items. The printed proofs are transcribed first (Part I); Part II is the complete numbered proof of the exact frozen statement LipschitzExtension ∧ Rademacher, following the printed route.

PART I. PRINTED PROOFS (cleaned transcription).

Theorem 1.2. If A is a non-empty subset of X and f : A → ℝ is Lipschitz, then there is f̄ : X → ℝ with Lip f̄ = Lip f and f = f̄|A.
Proof (printed). With L = Lip f, we claim that f̄(x) = inf_{z∈A} (f(z) + L d(x,z)), x ∈ X, has the required properties. Indeed if x ∈ A then trivially f̄(x) ≤ f(x) and also f̄(x) − f(x) = inf_{z∈A}(f(z) − f(x) + L d(x,z)) ≥ inf_{z∈A}(−L d(x,z) + L d(x,z)) = 0, so f̄(x) = f(x). Also for any x1, x2 ∈ X, f̄(x1) − f̄(x2) = sup_{z2∈A} inf_{z1∈A}(f(z1) + L d(x1,z1) − f(z2) − L d(x2,z2)) ≤ sup_{z2∈A}(L d(x1,z2) − L d(x2,z2)) ≤ L d(x1,x2), and the reverse inequality holds by interchanging x1, x2.

Theorem 1.4 (Rademacher). If f is Lipschitz on ℝⁿ then f is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e.
Proof (printed, due to C. B. Morrey). For v ∈ S^{n−1} let D_v f(x) = d/dt f(x+tv)|_{t=0} whenever it exists. Since |f(y)−f(x)|/|y−x| ≤ Lip f, |D_v f| ≤ Lip f, and D_v f(x) exists exactly when limsup_{t→0} and liminf_{t→0} of (f(x+tv)−f(x))/t coincide; both are Borel (limits of lower/upper semicontinuous sup/inf over 0<|t|<1/j), so A_v = {x : D_v f(x) does not exist} is Borel. For fixed x, v the function t ↦ f(x+tv) is absolutely continuous, hence differentiable for a.e. t, so A_v meets every line parallel to v in an H¹-null set, and by Fubini Lⁿ(A_v) = 0, i.e. (1) D_v f exists a.e. For φ ∈ C¹_c(ℝⁿ) and h > 0, (2) ∫ (f(x+hv)−f(x))/h · φ(x) dx = ∫ (φ(x)−φ(x−hv))/h · f(x) dx (change of variables), and by dominated convergence and (1), (3) ∫ D_v f φ = −∫ f D_v φ = −∫ f v·∇φ = Σ_j v^j ∫ D_j f φ = ∫ v·∇f φ, using Fubini and absolute continuity on lines for the integration by parts. Since φ is arbitrary, (4) D_v f(x) = v·∇f(x) for a.e. x, for each v, and (5) |∇f(x)| = sup_{|v|=1} D_v f(x) ≤ L at such points. With v_1, v_2, … dense in S^{n−1} and A_k = {x : ∇f(x), D_{v_k} f(x) exist and D_{v_k} f(x) = v_k·∇f(x)}, A = ∩_k A_k has (6) Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A) = 0. For x ∈ A, v ∈ S^{n−1}, h ≠ 0 put (7) Q(x,v,h) = (f(x+hv)−f(x))/h − v·∇f(x); then (8) Q(x,v_j,h) → 0 as h → 0. Given ε > 0 choose P with (9) S^{n−1} ⊆ ∪_{i≤P} B_ε(v_i) and δ_i with (10) 0 < |h| < δ_i ⇒ |Q(x,v_i,h)| < ε. For v ∈ S^{n−1} pick i ≤ P with |v−v_i| < ε; then |Q(x,v,h)| ≤ |Q(x,v,h)−Q(x,v_i,h)| + |Q(x,v_i,h)| ≤ |h|^{−1}|f(x+hv)−f(x+hv_i)| + |v−v_i||∇f(x)| + |Q(x,v_i,h)| < (2L+1)ε for 0 < |h| < δ = min δ_i, by (5). Hence f is differentiable at every x ∈ A.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF THE FROZEN STATEMENT.

Notation. For a map g between pseudo-(e)metric spaces, lipConst g = sInf {K ∈ ℝ≥0 : LipschitzWith K g} (the contract definition; it is literally the same expression as the SimonGMT definition Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.optimalLipschitzConstant, so the two are definitionally equal).

A. Theorem 1.2 (LipschitzExtension).
1. Let X be a metric space, A ⊆ X nonempty, f : A → ℝ with LipschitzWith K₀ f for some K₀ (A carries the subspace metric, dist(a,b) = d(a,b)). Put L := lipConst f.
2. f is L-Lipschitz (the infimum is attained). The set S = {K : LipschitzWith K f} is nonempty (K₀ ∈ S) and upward closed. For a, b ∈ A the inequality |f a − f b| ≤ K d(a,b) holds for every K ∈ S; choosing K_j ∈ S with K_j → L = inf S (property of the infimum in ℝ≥0) and letting j → ∞ gives |f a − f b| ≤ L d(a,b). (This is Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.lipschitzWith_optimalLipschitzConstant.)
3. Define F(x) := inf_{a∈A} (f(a) + L d(x,a)) for x ∈ X. The infimum is finite: fixing a₀ ∈ A (A ≠ ∅), for every a ∈ A, f(a) + L d(x,a) ≥ f(a₀) − L d(a,a₀) + L d(x,a) ≥ f(a₀) − L d(x,a₀) by step 2 and the triangle inequality, so the set of values is bounded below and nonempty.
4. F = f on A: for x ∈ A, choosing a = x gives F(x) ≤ f(x); and for every a ∈ A, f(a) + L d(x,a) ≥ f(x) by step 2, so F(x) ≥ f(x).
5. F is L-Lipschitz: for x1, x2 ∈ X and a ∈ A, f(a) + L d(x1,a) ≤ f(a) + L d(x2,a) + L d(x1,x2); taking the infimum over a gives F(x1) ≤ F(x2) + L d(x1,x2), and symmetrically F(x2) ≤ F(x1) + L d(x1,x2). Hence LipschitzWith L F; in particular ∃ K, LipschitzWith K F.
6. lipConst F = L. (≤) L belongs to {K : LipschitzWith K F} by step 5, so the infimum lipConst F ≤ L. (≥) If LipschitzWith K F then for a, b ∈ A, |f a − f b| = |F a − F b| ≤ K d(a,b) by step 4, i.e. LipschitzWith K f, so K ≥ lipConst f = L; taking the infimum over such K gives lipConst F ≥ L.
7. Steps 4-6 give the three required conclusions. (Formal route: the SimonGMT theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.lipschitz_extension_real_optimal (hA : A.Nonempty) (f : A → ℝ) (hf : IsLipschitz f) returns exactly F with IsLipschitz F (= ∃ K, LipschitzWith K F), F x = f x on A, and optimalLipschitzConstant F = optimalLipschitzConstant f; these are the frozen conclusions after unfolding the definitionally equal names. Alternatively Mathlib's LipschitzOnWith.extend_real applied to the function x ↦ (if h : x ∈ A then f ⟨x,h⟩ else 0), which is L-Lipschitz on A, gives F with LipschitzWith L F and F = f on A, and step 6 finishes.)

B. Theorem 1.4 (Rademacher).
8. Let n ∈ ℕ and f : ℝⁿ → ℝ with LipschitzWith K f, where ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and Lⁿ = volume.
9. Lebesgue measure volume on the finite-dimensional real normed space ℝⁿ is an additive Haar measure.
10. Morrey's argument of Part I proves that the set of points where f is not Fréchet differentiable is Lⁿ-null: steps (1)-(6) produce a full-measure set A on which the gradient ∇f and the directional derivatives along a countable dense set of directions exist and agree with v·∇f, and steps (7)-(10) show that at every x ∈ A the difference quotients converge to v·∇f(x) uniformly in v ∈ S^{n−1}, which is Fréchet differentiability with derivative h ↦ ∇f(x)·h.
11. This argument is formalized in Mathlib as LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt (file Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Rademacher.lean): for a Lipschitz map between finite-dimensional real normed spaces and any additive Haar measure μ on the source, ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x. (SimonGMT re-exports it as Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt.) Applying it with μ = volume (step 9) gives ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x, which is the conjunct Rademacher.
12. Steps 1-7 prove LipschitzExtension and steps 8-11 prove Rademacher; hence LipschitzExtension ∧ Rademacher.
proof_key_steps: Take L = lipConst f; the infimum of Lipschitz constants is attained, so f is L-Lipschitz.
Define the McShane extension F(x) = inf over a in A of f(a) + L d(x,a); it is finite because A is nonempty.
F = f on A and F is L-Lipschitz, so lipConst F ≤ L; restricting any constant of F to A gives lipConst f ≤ lipConst F (SimonGMT lipschitz_extension_real_optimal).

Rademacher: Morrey argument (directional derivatives a.e., weak gradient, uniformity over a dense set of directions), formalized as Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt for the add-Haar measure volume.

audit.reason: Both statements match the frozen conjunction. The optimal McShane extension argument and compatible, axiom-checked Haar-measure Rademacher theorem prove the exact conclusions without circularity.
